We analyze causal-decoder VLAs on LIBERO only; flow-matching~\cite{black2024_pi0} and diffusion~\cite{ghosh2024_octo} architectures may differ.
Trained $\Delta R^2$ correlates with published success rates ($\rho = 0.583$, $p = 0.10$; Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_discussion_appendix}) but the sample is underpowered ($n = 9$); tracing when collapse emerges during training remains for future work.

\paragraph{Practical implications.}
$\Delta R^2$ provides a cheap diagnostic (one forward pass plus probe): $> 0.10$ signals VLM-to-VLA reorganization; a flat profile indicates pre-existing action structure.
Preserved exit structure in VLA-to-VLA conditions justifies staged pipelines (OXE pretrain $\to$ task finetune); mid-layer probes outperform exit-layer probes where collapse is pronounced (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_discussion_appendix}).

\paragraph{Conclusion.}
Across three architectures and four LIBERO suites, VLM-to-VLA fine-tuning produces exit collapse ($\Delta R^2 = 0.15$--$0.45$) while VLA-to-VLA conditions remain flat ($< 0.10$).
All trained VLAs show graded counterfactual sensitivity ($d = 0.45$--$1.52$); L1 instruction attention is inherited from pretrained backbones; NLP controls ($\Delta R^2 = 0.000$) confirm transition-type specificity.
The exit-collapse diagnostic and reference-checkpoint protocol offer reusable evaluation tools; understanding which representational structures transfer and which must be constructed can inform more efficient VLA training.
Code and data will be released upon acceptance.
